extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting papers to ACL Rolling Review (ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on submitting papers to ACL Rolling Review: scope, formatting, anonymity, responding to reviews, resubmission, commitment to venues, and related procedural policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and suitability for ARR
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR provides reviews—and only reviews—for submissions. The standards expected by reviewers are those of a traditional direct submission as a long or short main conference paper to ACL (or the other major conferences operated by the ACL). Refer to the CFP for the scope and requirements to the submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System demonstrations should NOT be submitted to ARR. If you intend to send your paper to a workshop or to a more specialized conference (CoNLL, *SEM, INLG, etc.) check whether it is listed on the venues page. Some venues are hybrid and will consider ARR-reviewed papers as well as direct submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a submission deadline every two months: see dates and venues. Deadlines are firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to have a look at the submission form and responsible NLP checklist before submitting. In case of system instability it is recommended to submit at least one hour before the deadline. You may edit all aspects of your submission up until the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author reviewer-signup requirement (starting May 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in May 2025, all submitting authors have to also sign up as reviewers (deadline: 48h after the submission deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, all authors must complete the author registration form within 48h of the deadline. If they get assignments, any assigned reviews and metareviews must be completed on time. Emergency declaration procedures exist for emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must adhere to the formatting in the submission templates, which is available as an Overleaf template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided templates to avoid technical violations that could lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and editability
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are made in OpenReview. All authors will receive a confirmation email upon submission. You may edit all aspects of your submission up until the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of system instability it is recommended to submit at least one hour before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous preprint option and anonymization policy
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of submission you may opt to have ARR publish your paper as an anonymous preprint. These will remain anonymous during and after the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR follows the ACL Policies for Review and Citation. Submissions must be properly anonymized as detailed in the CFP. Beginning Feb 15, 2024 there is no anonymity period or limitation on posting or discussing non-anonymous preprints while the work is under peer review. Confidential comments in OpenReview are visible to ACs, SACs, and PCs—do not include author names or any identifying details in confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Under-review exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you have submitted your paper, and until you receive the meta-review, it will be considered under review by ARR. You may not submit the paper elsewhere during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the paper is no longer under review (after meta-review), you are free to commit it to a venue that accepts ARR reviews, submit it to some other venue, or resubmit to ARR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: You may withdraw your submission during the under-review period (before it receives a meta-review), but if you do so more than 48 hours after the submission deadline, your paper will be ineligible for resubmission in the next cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To withdraw, use OpenReview. Withdrawal has consequences: earlier reviewed versions also become ineligible for commitment, and it will not be possible to resubmit to ARR without restoring the withdrawn submission. If authors received even one review for it, it would still count as a resubmission and must be disclosed with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission may be desk rejected if it does not adhere to the CFP (e.g., if it is not in scope, if it violates technical submission requirements, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desk rejection can occur at any point in the review cycle, even after receiving initial reviews or a meta-review, if a technical violation is discovered. A desk-rejected version does not count as a prior submission for resubmission purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for irresponsible reviewers and chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers or area chairs who receive assignments but act irresponsibly will not be allowed to (re-)submit or commit their work during the current and the next ARR cycle. Teams of papers with such reviewers/chairs as authors will have to sit out a cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting authors should ensure all co-authors are aware of this policy and check that everybody submits their (meta-)reviews on time and according to guidelines. More details at the incentives2025 policy link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response purpose and high-level constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of author response at ARR is different from that at conferences: ARR is only a reviewing platform and reviewers do not have a direct say in acceptance decisions. The author response is not mandatory and should focus on clarifying misunderstandings or factual inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If clarity-related objections are raised, it might be best to revise and resubmit. If a reviewer has strong unfair objections, consider resubmitting and requesting different reviewers. Do not repeatedly argue with strongly opinionated reviewers; focus on main issues that significantly impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response allowed content and format restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your response must be text-only, and no external links are allowed. The paper will be desk-rejected if this is violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is OK to present new experimental results that are in direct response to a reviewer’s question — only minor add-ons such as a new ablation or different hyperparameter setting. You are not allowed to submit unsolicited new results indicating substantial additional work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response length and AC attention
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unreasonable to expect ACs to read very long discussions with reviewers: their guidelines ask them to read at least 2 author responses per review thread, but they will probably not read more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep discussions focused on main issues. The recommended length of the discussion at ARR is maximum 2 author responses per review thread; ACs are not obligated to read more than that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on interacting with reviewers (etiquette and escalation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not obligated to respond to author comments; they are only asked to update their review for factual misunderstandings or to correct guideline violations. Sending many reminders to non-responsive reviewers is not recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers violate guidelines, refer to specific points from ARR reviewer guidelines and flag issues via the review issue report form if unresolved. Asking reviewers to raise scores is not recommended and not automatically grounds for a confidential comment to the AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review issue reporting mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: After the author discussion period, authors can report review issues using a form with 12 issue types (I1-I12). The review issue reporting mechanism should be used only when the reviewer has not done due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most issue types (except I5, I8-9, I11-12) are referenced in the ARR reviewer guidelines. When flagging issues, authors should provide justification. The meta-review form contains checkboxes for ACs to specify whether reported review issues were taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review issue reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Dec 2024, it is possible to report issues with meta-reviews for procedural issues or serious violations of ARR policies. This mechanism is not for arguing against reasonable differences of perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For MI3, the report should be backed up by references to specific guidelines/policies. These reports signal a problem to senior chairs but do not trigger a revision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review options and mutual exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: After final reviews and a meta-review, authors can: quickly revise and submit a new revision for the next ARR deadline (~1 week), submit to a subsequent deadline (2+ months), commit the reviews to an ARR venue, or submit for direct (non-ARR) review by a venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options are mutually exclusive: you cannot submit a revision and in parallel commit to a venue. Check CFP for rules on dual submissions. Reviewer feedback and scores do not directly indicate acceptance; different venues have different qualitative thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment process and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment occurs through a submission form set up by the PCs of the venue and asks for information including the ARR URL. After the commitment deadline, ARR provides the reviews to the venue and they make a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR does not place restrictions on committing to multiple venues simultaneously, but venues typically do not permit dual commitments/submissions. The commitment phase ends when the paper is no longer under consideration by any venue. If accepted, submitting camera-ready accepts the publication offer and paper can no longer be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional response to meta-review guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the venue provides an optional 'response to the meta-review' field, it is up to authors to decide whether to use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible uses: summarize revision history, outline changes you commit to for camera-ready, summarize serious procedural meta-review issue and link to comment, briefly respond to a new issue raised only in the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To resubmit you must submit the same information as Step 1, plus: the link to your previous submission, an explanation of revisions responding to prior reviews, and preferences regarding reviewers and the meta-reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation of revisions should be a PDF and may include a color-coded version of the paper to make changes easier to see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of revisions content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation of revisions should summarize changes and include a point-by-point response indicating how you addressed each weakness and suggestion (or justifications for not doing some revisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including a color-coded version, use different colors for content that is actually new vs content moved from other parts. Engage with reviewers’ constructive feedback; ignoring good advice is not recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission frequency and novelty threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: You can resubmit a paper as many times as you like. When presented as a new submission, it must be on a sufficiently different topic that any prior reviews no longer apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply reframing the paper, further improving methods, or adding baselines/analysis does not count as a new submission. A paper previously submitted but failing to acknowledge the previous version will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment for resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can request same or new reviewers and preferences regarding meta-reviewer when resubmitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR will attempt to reassign the same reviewers if requested, but availability may require new reviewers. New reviewers will not see the prior reviews initially; only after they submit their own review. Repeat reviewers are instructed to focus on whether revisions adequately address previously identified weaknesses and are discouraged from raising new issues unless revisions introduce contradictory findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC option to remove very low-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: In rare cases where a very low-quality review was flagged by authors, Area Chairs have the option to recommend that a specific review is removed from view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary and intended for clearly unacceptably low-quality reviews identified via the review issue mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The limitations section should focus on the soundness of the study and answer: what methodological caveats should the reader be aware of when interpreting findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: convenience sampling of models/languages/data, potential confounding factors (e.g., LLM test data contamination), practical limitations like high compute intensity. State clearly what was done, where findings may not hold, and what future work would be needed to test those directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on dissertations as prior publications
rubrics_metrics.description: University dissertations and theses do not count as prior publications for the purposes of ARR submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to the paper and review dataset (opt-in consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission form asks if authors agree for the anonymized metadata associated with a submission to be included in a publicly available dataset. The ARR data collection is voluntary and requires consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review metadata (scores, anonymous reviewer identifiers) will only be included if both authors and reviewers agree. Submission and review texts are handled separately. Authors of accepted papers will be contacted with instructions on donating peer review reports to an open public dataset; only one author needs to sign the license agreement on behalf of co-authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting reviewers for collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a review was helpful and you wish to reach out to the reviewer for collaboration, contact the ARR editors specifying the forum link and reviewer ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will reach out on your behalf and, if the reviewer agrees, put you in touch with them.
